transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-24 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Arjun (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood Solutions), Lina (Stratus PM), Rob (Stratus Eng lead), Sana (Stratus Security), Tom (Stratus SRE)

Auto-summary (auto):
- Quick POC check-in focused on SDK invoke adapters, function-calling failure modes, and tightening the structured-output schema for billing ingestion.
- Action items: run KV-cache microbench, share latency/cost tradeoff sheet, customer to validate schema on staging.

Topics noted: SDK adapters, function/tool calling, schema validation, graceful degradation, security/KMS, on-prem checklist

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick call, we'll run through the integration pain points you flagged and the recent results.
[00:14] Lina: thanks maya, yeah a few things from our side - the billing pipeline is sensitive to small schema variances so we hit a couple rejects in staging yesterday.
[00:28] Rob: mmhmm, we had a few responses where the SDK returned 'null' for the charge_code field and then the downstream parser blew up, so want to make sure the structured output enforce is tighter.
[00:45] Arjun: ok got it, can you paste one of those failing responses in the thread? that helps us repro. sometimes it's a prompt edge where function calling turned into free text.
[00:58] Rob: yeah i'll drop the sample in the doc after this. it looked like the model chose to emit plain text rather than call the tool schema.
[01:12] Maya: quick question for the team, are you currently pinning to hosted Redwood or trying Dedicated for the POC? i remember timeline was leaning dedicated if perf checked out.
[01:24] Lina: we started with hosted to move fast but we want to move to dedicated if quantization and batching don't cause regressions. also the security team is asking about VPC and KMS options.
[01:37] Sana: yep from Sec we need to confirm KMS integration, HSM availability unclear, and SOC2 artifact access for the audit.
[01:46] Diego: just to note, Redwood Private supports customer KMS via cloud KMS/HSM and we can walk through the on-prem checklist. we'll put the security doc link in the notes.
[02:03] Tom: latency is a big factor for us. when we switched to batched calls in staging we saw tail latency spikes at 99th that affected our workers. do you have tuning recommendations?
[02:18] Arjun: yes, what we usually do is a hybrid: small continuous batching for tail smoothing plus prefix KV caching for repeated invocations. caching cuts token work and avoids full re-eval.
[02:32] Lina: can you quantify that in our profile? our typical prompt sizes are 180-320 tokens, with a 1.2 requests/sec per user.
[02:45] Arjun: based on that distribution we expect batching to reduce per-token cost by ~18-28% with minor avg latency increase, but tail latency depends on your burst pattern. i'll run a microbenchmark against a similar seq len and share numbers.
[02:58] Rob: loss in determinism is risky for billing schema though; if caching causes slight permutations in the output shape it breaks us.
[03:14] Arjun: right, the runtime ensures schema stability if you use function-calling enforced mode. issue arises when the model opts out or hallucinate fields. we recommend a required function signature so the model has to return structured JSON.
[03:34] Lina: we tried that but still saw one case where the model returned a top-level string and not the object. maybe a prompt framing issue.
[03:45] Maya: that's when we suggest the schema validation layer in the SDK: you can register a schema and the SDK will either coerce or flag the output, and optionally retry with a tighter prompt.
[03:58] Rob: is that retry synchronous? our pipeline is sensitive to added latency.
[04:08] Arjun: retries are configurable. you can set it to do a single automatic re-prompt with augmented instruction, or surface an error upstream and fall back to a deterministic legacy path.
[04:22] Tom: what about graceful degradation? if the model is slow or returns invalid, we want a deterministic fallback response so invoicing doesn't block.
[04:33] Diego: we support fallback policies: route to smaller quantized model, or fallback to cached last-known-good answer, or to a rule-based fallback. policies can be set per-route in the console.
[04:48] Lina: okay that helps. one open question: when you do quantized models for cost, do you see more schema drift?
[04:58] Arjun: small increases in hallucination risk with aggressive quant, but we have quant-profile recommendations per workload; for structured outputs we usually use medium quant or mixed int8 for prompt-heavy workloads.
[05:12] Rob: on the SDK integration we hit a mismatch in the tool interface: our adapter layer expects tool responses as a flat key map, but the SDK emits nested objects for some tools.
[05:25] Maya: can you describe the adapter contract you have now? is it the Redwood SDK wrapper or your own shim?
[05:33] Rob: it's our shim. we call the SDK, then we map fields into internal objects. the problem was when the model invoked a tool with array outputs and we flattened it incorrectly.
[05:45] Arjun: ok two things: 1) the SDK has a 'tool_adapter' hook where you can register a mapping function to normalize outputs before they hit your shim; 2) we can add a strict-mode that rejects non-conforming tool outputs so you get early failure.
[06:02] Lina: sweet. can you enable that strict-mode in staging for our project id?
[06:10] Maya: yes we can flip that flag for the pilot to help surface failures.
[06:15] Rob: another weird one - function-calling failures when sequence length was near token limit; the model would truncate and then emit incomplete JSON.
[06:27] Arjun: that's expected with hard token limits. options: increase model max context (bigger instance), use streaming with partial result assembly, or do aggressive prompt truncation plus stateful KV cache to keep only relevant context.
[06:44] Tom: streaming seems promising; but we need to reassemble and run schema validation incrementally which is non-trivial.
[06:53] Diego: we have an SDK example for incremental JSON assembly - i'll link it. it's not perfect but it covers partial chunks and rehydrates the object.
[07:06] Lina: yes please share that example. also, can you share the sample latency csv you mentioned earlier?
[07:13] Arjun: i'll push the microbench csv and a trimmed dashboard view to the shared folder after this call.
[07:20] Maya: quick pause, let's talk about security items san a raised - KMS and audit logs.
[07:27] Sana: we need: KMS integration details, proof of key handling (who holds keys), retention windows for logs, and SSO/SAML support for RBAC. also where are audit logs stored for Private vs Hosted?
[07:43] Diego: for Private they stay in your VPC, for Hosted we keep logs for the default retention window but we can export to customer S3 with encryption; we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning.
[07:55] Sana: can you share a short checklist for SOC2 evidence?
[08:00] Maya: yes we'll share the security pack link (redwood.com/sec/pilot-pack) and a short SOC2 artifact list.
[08:10] Rob: a question on pricing - if we use dedicated with burst, how are tokens billed when we fall back to hosted?
[08:22] Maya: billing depends on route: dedicated committed capacity covers calls routed to your pool; fallback to hosted is billed at standard hosted per-token rates and we show a per-route cost breakdown in the console so you can monitor. we'll include an example invoice calc.
[08:37] Lina: good. on sequencing, we want to lock acceptance criteria: 1) structured output schema validated in staging with <0.1% rejects, 2) latency p99 under 1.1s for typical flows, 3) security checklist agreed. target end-of-poc date is 2026-12-15.
[08:58] Maya: sounds reasonable, we'll map tasks.
[09:05] Rob: practical ask - can you add a test harness we can run in CI that simulates 2000 low concurrency events to surface schema regressions?
[09:18] Arjun: yes, we have a small harness we can share; it uses the SDK and replay tool calls, will add as a repo link.
[09:27] Tom: on the CI harness, make sure it can toggle strict-mode and simulate retries.
[09:34] Arjun: noted.
[09:37] (crosstalk) Lina: quick note: we'll validate the schema using jsonschema and share results by friday.
[09:44] Rob: i'll post the malformed outputs and a unit-level test failing stacktrace.
[09:50] Diego: regarding the KV-cache benchmark — one caveat is cache invalidation semantics when you have multi-tenant keys; we'll provide recommended keying patterns.
[10:05] Rob: good, we need a pattern for tokenization of customer ids in the key to avoid collisions.
[10:13] Arjun: recommended: route-key = project-id + intent-hash, keep TTL short for billing flows.
[10:21] Lina: that should work.
[10:25] Maya: wrapping up, recap of next steps and owners: Arjun bench, Maya pricing + security pack, Rob tests and malformed outputs, Sana compliance questions, Diego share SDK incremental JSON example.
[10:41] Lina: ok thanks all, can we reconvene next Tuesday same time for a short elide?
[10:48] Maya: yes i'll send invite for 2026-12-01 15:00 UTC.

End of transcript.
